limitations: Development splits only; warm in-process queries, three fresh processes/stores per arm, one 2-vCPU m7a.large host; no heldout or SOTA acceptance.
Local engine stores and search APIs, not hosted HTTP/S3/KMS execution, customer authentication, host/AZ failover or product pricing.
Native materializes a public paged RecordLog view and builds a fresh projection with excerpts per query; baselines retain indexes; actual API work differs.

The local adapter has native 100k-record/128-MiB state bounds. Hosted captured-record projection has separate 4k-selected-record/8-MiB limits; these larger local workloads establish no hosted capacity claim.
Native/Nine ranking differs from FTS5/Tantivy; query quality and returned-original byte counts accompany latency.
SWE-agent relevance is lexically generated, not independent human judgment; BEIR ArguAna uses its published judgments.
Full file apparent/allocated sizes are verified against the AWS archive; directory inode/filesystem metadata and external dependencies are outside those metrics.
Off-host cold reopen checks integrity in fresh processes using copied stores; OS page caches were not dropped and no cold-cache latency claim is made.
Turnloop raw_text_bytes excludes the synthetic canary text; full-store byte counts include canaries. Exact cold-read text-byte totals include every stored original.
Public fixed sealing key and explicit benchmark imported clocks do not establish production confidentiality or native ingest-clock claims.
Tantivy largest-history ranking determinism failure is retained and disqualifies that scorecard from performance claims.
Approximately $0.249 for two hours is a compute/IPv4/32-GiB-gp3 estimate, excluding S3/Scheduler/transfer/tax; not an AWS bill or customer price.
